Tina Kotek

Democrat, Working Families candidate for Governor, Oregon · Incumbent

Governor of Oregon

Tina Kotek is the Democratic Governor of Oregon and has held the office since January 2023, after defeating Christine Drazan in 2022. She announced her reelection campaign in December 2025. She is on the November 3, 2026 ballot as the Democratic nominee, also listed as the Working Families nominee, in a rematch with Drazan.

Where Kotek stands

Housing and homelessness
Says she has made housing permits faster, cut red tape and funded infrastructure. Cites an 11.5% year-over-year rise in Oregon housing starts as evidence of progress.
Affordability and utility costs
Signed the POWER Act, which lets state regulators set separate rates for large power users like data centers. Says the law lowers household utility costs by making data centers pay their fair share.
Data centers
Supports a moratorium on new data center development in Oregon.
Early childhood education
Proposes universal preschool across Oregon in a second term.
K-12 education
Proposes cutting absences, raising classroom time to the national average by the end of a second term, tightening diploma requirements and limiting social media on school devices. Supports early literacy (science of reading) programs.
Economy and jobs
Proposes replacing the state's economic development agency with a new Department of Commerce, recruiting investment in renewable energy and biosciences, and making more land ready for development.
Health care and food assistance
Pledges to protect Oregonians from federal cuts to the Oregon Health Plan and food assistance, and to work to bring federal tax dollars back to Oregon.
Immigration enforcement
Opposes aggressive enforcement of federal immigration laws in Oregon.
Elections and voting
Pledges to fight attempts to change Oregon's mail-in voting system.
Federal administration
Opposed the National Guard deployment in Portland and the freeze of SNAP benefits during the federal government shutdown.

Background

  • Governor of Oregon, 2023–present
  • Speaker of the Oregon House of Representatives, 2013–2022
  • Oregon State Representative, 2007–2022
  • Democratic nominee for Governor, 2022 (won the general election against Christine Drazan)
